description.narrative: The Love Alliance, a new five-year programme (2021-2025), is based on an unwavering commitment to protecting, promoting and fulfilling sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) globally, unifying people who use drugs, sex workers and LGBTIQ+ movements, and amplifying the diversity of voices in these communities. Funded by the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Love Alliance brings together national thought leaders GALZ, SANPUD and Sisonke, regional grantmakers UHAI EASHRI, GNP+, ISDAO and ARASA with the global network of people living with HIV (GNP+) and the Netherlands-based administrative lead Aidsfonds. Together, we advocate for adequate levels of funding and for taking truly human rights-based programmes to scale. We take this opportunity to prioritise and invest in challenging the structural barriers of underfunding, criminalisation and exclusion of us in all our diversity.

description.narrative: The Trans Health Centre etsablished has had a profound impact on the trans community in Morocco since its establishment in 2024. Serving 110 unique beneficiaries over the past year, with 25-30 individuals accessing services monthly, the clinic has become a lifeline for many trans people in Morocco. By offering critical services like hormonal transition care, HIV/STI testing, and PrEP access, the center addresses a glaring gap in trans-inclusive healthcare. According to testimonies in TDs report, for many, it is the only safe space where they can receive competent, respectful care without fear of discrimination, stigma or neglect. The clinic has been particularly transformative for trans people living with HIV, who face unique challenges in managing their health and getting consultation and advice from a health professional and friendly.

description.narrative: The grantee has organised three workshop series for PLHIV and LGBTQI communities. According to the report, The Mental Health, Religion, and Spirituality Workshop fostered stronger collaborations with mental health professionals, promoting community support amongst participants and reducing stigma and discrimination from health services and self-stigma for community members.The Empowering Identities Workshop equipped trans individuals with self-advocacy skills, strengthening resilience and collective action and cross-movement solidarity.

comment.narrative: # of civil society organisations with increased capacity to advocate for the rights of key populations

National partners workshop organised by GNP+ in Casablanca Morocco that aimed at connecting partners, introducing partners to Love Alliance advocacy loop and ToC, equipping partners with tools to effectively manage and report on their activities financially, and to assess the actual context in which they operate through identifying the strength, weakness, opportunities and threats faced by each partner organisation. New partners were engaged through a peer-led participatory grantmaking process where their capacity on activities and expenditure planning was strengthened through our budget and work plan co-build processes.
